npcs.summary:
The cast is in. All 31 characters from bible §2 are defined, plus the three gate aunties, about 40 walk-ons and the special speakers (radio, crowd, chit, email, immu_tape, imran_tape). Every speaker id used in the bible's 476 dialogue lines is registered in N.dialogue.speakers. tests/npcs.cjs passes all 40 checks in strict mode with zero console errors, and tests/smoke.cjs passes on desktop, portrait and landscape.

**Characters.** Each one has a name-plate colour, a voice pitch, a sprite look and a hand-painted pixel portrait. Sprites get hats, beards, specs, ponytails, plaits and hand props (Pasha's antenna, Patang Chacha's charkhi, Salim's tray, Amma's chappal and so on) by wrapping N.people.draw from npcs.js; entities.js is untouched.
- 2026 versions exist for Srikanth, Imran, Amma, Nanna, Rasheed-saab, Ayesha and Faramarz. They switch on when N.flags.year is 2026, N.flags.year2026 is set, or seasons reports year2026.
- Outfit variants: Chinnu in school uniform, Immu's Chand Raat raincoat (switches on by itself on Chand Raat), Amma's night clothes, chappal in hand or Bonalu pot, Ramulu as Pothuraju (switches on by itself at Bonalu), Rasheed-saab's Chand Raat cap, Bunty's committee badge.
- The player gets Chinnu's look (Srikanth in 2026) on new game, load and when the year changes.

**Runtime.**
- spawn() adds a "Talk to <name>" ACTION at priority 3. Places on a roof use the world agent's roof zones, so Patang Chacha stands on his roof.
- walkTo follows the road graph for long trips and a grid path for short ones, re-planning when blocked. Tested from 142u up to about 1270u with no stuck hops while on screen and never off walkable ground. During a mission the promise rejects with MissionAbort when that mission ends.
- follow(): Immu keeps up on foot, gets on his own red cycle when the player rides, and gets off when the player does. His parked cycle can't be borrowed.
- driveTo: Yadagiri drove his labelled auto from Koti to Sultan Bazaar.
- Also lookAt, face, 10 emote bubbles, and short spoken lines when the player passes.

**Regulars on by default.** The three aunties on the playground_1 cement bench ("Ask aunty" asks storycore for a hint), Faramarz at irani_cafe_19, Patang Chacha on patang_chacha_roof, the shopkeepers, Ammamma on the home verandah (hint source 'home'), Bahadur at night, Pochaiah on the RTC X Roads podium (hidden while the Chappal Meter is 3 or more), Cable Babji, Tiger and Vimala Ma'am. Immu's post-game hangout and Ayesha's dawn nets are off until the story turns them on. Which schedules are on is saved.

**dialogue.js.**
- Name tokens {nick}, {NICK}, {full}, {FULL} plus the bible's rename rule ("Chinnu", "chinnu_" email ids, "Srikanth"). It reads the fields the menus name card writes, and filter is also exported as subst for storycore.
- Glossary has 389 keys covering bible §10 and systems §17 with phrase matching; every slang word in the bible's lines has a meaning. There is a hover tooltip and a meanings row under the line.
- 10 moods with tinted backgrounds and marks. Chinnu/Srikanth speak from the right, everyone else from the left. Tape, radio, chit and email lines get their own box style.
- Every bible line and choice fits on a 390x844 phone (tallest box 290px) and in 844x390 landscape (tallest 223px).
- N.dialogue.bark(target, text) shows a speech bubble over the speaker in the world.
- N.dialogue.current.speaker still reports the id the script used ('you' stays 'you'), so the existing core_systems dialogue check passes.

The story bible's character section, my sprite looks and the procedural portraits are the parts most worth eyeballing in the cast sheets.
api_notes: Speaker ids = npc ids: chinnu srikanth amma nanna ammamma chitti bunty immu imran abba ammi nani ayesha pasha babloo faramarz pochaiah yadagiri ramulu agarwal bahadur kite_chacha ticket_thatha salim vimala_maam cable_babji photo_uncle net_uncle flower_aunty tiger caretaker aunty aunty_2 aunty_3 + walk-ons (bakery_man gokul_man paradise_man bawarchi_man conductor sentry mali watchman guide boatman farmer chemist painter ticket_man black_ticket narsimha chappal_man bangle_man attar_man recording_man coconut_man dosa_man stationery_man kirana_kid papad_man bird_man book_man bakery_lady meat_man uncle coach guard carol_aunty waiter banana_man) + loudspeaker radio crowd chit email immu_tape imran_tape narrator. 'you' resolves to chinnu (2003) / srikanth (2026). Use immu_tape / imran_tape for the bible's 'immu (tape):' lines.

N.npcs.spawn(id, target, {angle, idle:'stand'|'wander'|'sit'|'work', talk, label, key, r, off:[dx,dy], bench, roof:'<roof id>', vehicle, owner}) -> actor. target = place id | [ids] (first that exists) | landmark id | npc key | 'player' | {x,y} | [x,y] | entity. Re-spawning an existing key moves it. An unknown place spawns beside the player with one console.warn, never an error. Roof places (home_terrace, friend_terrace, patang_chacha_roof, lakshmi_t2..t6) go through N.world.roofs.place. talk: fn(actor, player) | string | [lines | {t, mood}] | false. Wrap with m.spawn(actor) so it despawns when the mission ends.

await N.npcs.walkTo(key, target, {run, speed, r, timeout, face}) -> true/false; inside a mission it rejects with MissionAbort when that mission ends. N.npcs.stop(key). await N.npcs.driveTo(key, target, {r, speed, timeout, vehicle}) drives the NPC's own vehicle along the roads.

N.npcs.follow(key, leader | null, {dist, side:'left'|'right'|'behind', ride: true | type, catchUp}): on foot, plus auto mount/dismount of the character's own vehicle (Immu: red Hero cycle; Bunty bunty_rx100 -> rx100; Nanna family_chetak -> chetak; Pochaiah pochaiah_luna -> luna; Pasha pasha_lambretta -> yellow chetak; Yadagiri yadagiri_auto -> auto; Narsimha peacock_lorry -> lorry). N.npcs.ride(key, type | vehicle) / dismount(key). NPC vehicles have noEnter set.

N.npcs.lookAt(key, target|null), face(key, target), emote(key, '!'|'?'|'♪'|'...'|'♥'|'!!'|'zzz'|'anger'|'sweat'|'*', secs), bark(key, text), say(key, text, opts), talkTo(key), setTalk(key, talk), setIdle(key, idle, {r, bench}), setLabel(key, label), get(key), all(), despawn(key|actor), list.

N.npcs.setVariant(id, name|null): chinnu 'school'|'camera', immu 'raincoat', amma 'night'|'chappal'|'bonam', ramulu 'pothuraju', abba 'chandraat', bunty 'committee'. Automatic: flags.chand_raat gives Immu the raincoat and Rasheed-saab the cap; flags.bonalu makes Ramulu the Pothuraju. Variants are not saved: the story sets them per mission. N.npcs.look(id) / portraitLook(id) return the current (variant/year-aware) looks, e.g. for wanted.js pursuers.

Schedules: N.npcs.schedule(name, on). Names: colony_aunties, faramarz, kite_chacha, shopkeepers, ammamma_swing, bahadur_night, pochaiah_podium, cable_babji, tiger_ground, vimala_school (on by default); immu_hangout, ayesha_nets (off). A key the story spawned itself is never touched by a schedule. Saved in section 'npcs'.

Hint hook (storycore): Ammamma's default talk shows N.hints.next('home').text, the gate aunties ('Ask aunty') N.hints.next('aunty').text, and Old City locals (kite_chacha, faramarz, bangle_man, attar_man, bird_man, chappal_man, papad_man) N.hints.next('city').text inside the Old City. With no active clue they say their own lines.

Dialogue: N.dialogue.say/choice/play take {mood, side, auto, style}. Moods: neutral happy laugh angry sad surprised shout worried wink tired (aliases grin, sulk, shock, cross, smug). N.dialogue.filter / subst(text), names(), setNames({nick, full}) (emits names:change), gloss(word), glossary, dictionary [{word, tag, meaning}] for the Journal, speakerName(id), bark(actor|id|{x,y}|'player', text, {secs, speaker, name, blip}) -> {close(), done}, clearBarks(), is2026(). current = {speaker (id the script used), as (resolved id), text, typing, choices, selected, mood}.

Events: npc:spawn {key, id, actor}, npc:despawn, npc:talk {key, id, actor}, npc:arrive {key, id}, dialogue:line {speaker, as, text, choices, mood}, dialogue:bark {speaker, text, target}. Player look: N.npcs.applyPlayerLook(); opt out with N.npcs.keepPlayerLook = true.

menus.summary:
The menus and cutscenes module (src/menus.js, about 3,000 lines) is built and working. tests/menus.cjs passes 216 checks across desktop 1280x720 (keyboard), portrait 390x844 (touch) and landscape 844x390 (touch), with zero console, page or N.err errors. tests/smoke.cjs passes on all three viewports.

What the player gets:
- **Title:** a cassette J-card in kid's handwriting over Charminar at dusk (clock 18:38), with the camera drifting slowly. It has the VHS OSD "■ STOP --:--", counter 000, and menu items written like track names: ▶ PLAY, ▶▶ CONTINUE (only when a save exists; shows "TRACK nn · date · ₹"), OTHER TAPE (when a manual save differs), VIEW (only when N.view exists), SETTINGS, CREDITS. PLAY calls N.audio.unlock() inside the click. If a save exists it first asks "Record over Side A?". On short landscape phones the card switches to two columns when there are five or more tracks so it still fits.
- **Name card:** a school exam-paper card, no prompt(). Nickname defaults to Chinnu (12 letters max), formal name to Srikanth with a fixed "K." initial. Letters and spaces only, live preview "Mummy shouts SRIKANTH!", and the on-screen keyboard opens on phones. Names are saved and survive newGame.
- **Pause:** a 2-in-1 cassette deck showing the date, time, tape counter, district and objective. Keys: Resume, Map, Journal, Settings, Save, Load, Quit mission (only during a mission), Quit to title (warns "Last saved N minutes ago" and offers Save & quit). Save is refused with the reason on screen during missions, minigames, cutscenes, dialogue, Chappal Meter 3 or more, or N.flags.no_save. Pause also works mid-dialogue and mid-cutscene; a paused cutscene holds its position.
- **Full map:** a 1999 city-guide style map drawn from world data (paper, red arterials, blue lake, rails, grid A–H by 1–6, district names in English and Telugu, road names). It pans and zooms by drag, pinch, wheel, arrow keys/WASD, +/− and gamepad, with three zoom levels. Every must-have place that exists in the world data has an icon (182 of 184; the other 2 aren't in world data yet). Shops are filterable by kind in the legend. Tapping a place opens a card with a route button. Waypoints are set by right-click, long-press or ACTION on empty ground, show as a pink route on the minimap, and clear on arrival. Collectible hiding spots never show.
- **Journal:** a "Mera Yaadgaar Saal" notebook with tabs:
  - Story so far: the bible diary lines with Vimala Ma'am's red ink and marks.
  - Side A: the J-card track list, read from N.tape.
  - The Tin: N.tape.tin.
  - The Lock: the brass dial plus the riddles.
  - Hyderabadi dictionary: 332 words with tags and search.
  - Other modules can add tabs; storycore's Clues tab already shows.
- **Settings:** sound volumes and mute (through N.audio), text speed, auto-advance, captions, reduced motion, flash reduction, VHS strength, high contrast, colour-blind blips, touch handedness and button size (CSS-only mirroring of the touch controls), the difficulty presets from systems §14.1, hint nudges, minigame assist, "Let Immu do it", storage status and a two-step erase. Everything persists and survives a reload.
- **Save/load:** the normal save slot (what CONTINUE loads) plus a separate manual copy written by the pause menu's Save. Loading the manual copy leaves the latest slot untouched.
- **Cutscene player:** every step type in ARCHITECTURE §19 plus extras (prompt, definitions, sfx, music, osd, counter, flash, title, letterbox, vhsfx). It has letterbox bars, a 1-second hold-to-skip (keyboard, pad or touch) and a SKIP pill; skipping still runs `call` steps. abortCutscene() resolves at once. It works in portrait and landscape and respects reduced motion.
- **Credits:** the bible §9.4 text scrolling on a J-card (hold E for 4x, Esc to leave; paged under reduced motion). Also the "NOSTALGIA (n.)" definitions card, a J-card line strip for MISSION PASSED, and an OSD "▶ PLAY" card shown after CONTINUE.

Integration fixes made along the way:
- Other modules read settings as plain properties (`N.settings.captions`, `.hintNudges`, `.letImmu`, `.difficulty`), so every setting is exposed that way, and `N.menus.settings` is an alias.
- Names are set on N.player.name/nick/full/fullName, and I use N.dialogue.setNames and N.dialogue.filter when they exist. I deliberately do not write names into N.flags.
- My Side A, Tin, Lock, Story and Dictionary tabs keep their ids, so storycore's duplicate side_a/tin tabs are ignored unless registered with replace:true.
- The 3D view mode (N.view, ARCHITECTURE §20) automatically gets the VIEW title track and a View row in settings.
- I added a "menus implementation notes" block to ARCHITECTURE §19.
api_notes: Engine hooks (unchanged contract): N.menus.title(), pause(), resume(), hideAll() (also aborts a running cutscene), isOpen(), plus openPause(). The PLAY button keeps id #title-start; the pause screen keeps class .pause-screen and [data-act=resume].

Names: await N.menus.nameEntry({nick, full}) returns {nick, full}, or null if the player backs out. Also names() -> {nick, full, FULL}, setNames(nick, full), subst(text) (uses N.dialogue.filter when present, else replaces {nick} {NICK} {full} {FULL}). Names live on N.player.name/nick/full/fullName, are saved in the save section 'profile', survive N.systems.reset(), and are remembered in localStorage 'nostalgia.profile.v1'.

Cutscenes: await N.menus.cutscene(steps, {id, skippable=true, letterbox=true, keepCamera, holdFade}) -> {skipped, aborted}. It pushes 'cutscene' when started from play, dialogue, minigame or gameover. Calls queue one after another. A bare function counts as a call step; any step with async:true runs alongside the next steps.

Step types: card {title, sub, ms, kind:'osd'|'chapter'|'title', te, ur, dim} (titles starting with ▶■◀●❚ use the OSD look) · text {lines|text, ms, dim, speaker} · vhs {mode:'rewind'|'ff'|'play'|'stop'|'rec'|'pause', ms, year:[2026,2003], label, amount, hold, music, sfx} · fade {to:'black'|'clear'|'white', ms} · wait {ms, advance} · say {s, t, mood, auto} · talk {lines} · camera {target: place/landmark/npc id | entity | {x,y} | [x,y], x, y, dx, dy, zoom, ms, release} · call {fn(ctx)} · jcard {id|track, title, place, scribble, line, counter, ms} · credits {} · definitions {} · prompt {label, hint} · sfx {name, x, y} · music {id|null, fade} · osd {text, sub, ms, hold} · counter {from, to, ms, side} · flash · title {title, sub, ms} · letterbox {on} · vhsfx {amount}.

Cutscene control: N.menus.abortCutscene() (missions.js already calls it), skipCutscene(), and the inCutscene getter. Events: cutscene:start {id}, cutscene:step {id, i, type}, cutscene:skip, cutscene:end {id, skipped, aborted}, and cutscene:vhs {mode, tape} (audio.js plays the rewind sound for it). Hold ACTION 1 s, hold the screen 1 s, or tap the SKIP pill to skip; a short ACTION or tap advances the current card or text.

Story screens: await N.menus.credits({fromTitle}) -> {left}; finishing credits outside the title sets N.flags.credits_seen. await N.menus.definitions() (bible §9.3, substitutes {full}). await N.menus.jcard({id: missionId}) shows the bible J-card line plus Immu's scribble and counter. N.menus.osdCard(text, {sub, ms}) is non-blocking.

Journal: N.menus.openJournal(tabId) / closeJournal() (mode 'journal'), addJournalTab({id, title, order, render(el, api), badge}), removeJournalTab(id), refreshJournal(), journalTabs(), addDiary({id, date, text, ink, mark}). Built-in tabs are story(10), side_a(20), tin(40), lock(50), dictionary(90); they are kept unless a caller passes replace:true (ignored ids are listed in N.menus.ignoredTabs).

Journal data it reads: N.tape.{counter, side, paused, tracks, tin, tokens[id] or tokenInfo(id), lock}, N.missions.isDone(id), N.flags.lock_1..lock_4 or lock_digit_N and riddle_N, N.flags.credits_seen together with N.story.replay(missionId) for the Replay button, and N.dialogue.dictionary or else N.dialogue.glossary. Bible fallback data is exported as N.menus.TRACKS, DIARY, TOKENS, LOCK, DEFINITIONS, CREDITS, MUST.

Map: N.menus.openMap({x, y, zoom:'city'|'district'|'near'|number}) / closeMap() (mode 'map'), addMapLayer({id, title, order, color, icon, points() -> [{x, y, icon, shape, glyph, color, label, id, done, faded, r}], draw(ctx, view)}), removeMapLayer(id). A layer with id 'collectibles' replaces the built-in one, which reads N.collectibles.items/has/isKnown. waypoint(x, y | null) uses the HUD blip 'mn:waypoint' with route:true. The place card also shows N.shops.hoursText(id), N.flags.visited_<id> and N.collectibles.triviaFor(id) when those exist. Test hooks: _mapIcons(), _mapHit(id).

Settings: N.settings.get/set/values/reset/diff(key)/textCps()/vhsScale()/apply(), and every key is also a plain property. Keys: textSpeed, autoAdvance, captions, reducedMotion, flashReduce, vhs, handed, btnSize, difficulty (relaxed|normal|hard), hintNudges (alias .hints), assist, letImmu, colorBlind, highContrast, mapLayers, mapKinds. diff() keys: pursuerSpeed sight unseenDrop chappalInterval homingTurn tummyDrain missionTimers cargoDamage minigameOffset caughtFine(paise) hintNudge. Emits settings:change. Body classes: reduced-motion, flash-reduce, touch-left, tbtn-s/tbtn-l, captions-on, high-contrast, cb-<mode>. Sets N.dialogue.textSpeed and N.dialogue.autoAdvance. Persisted in localStorage 'nostalgia.settings.v1' (wrapped in try/catch).

N.menus.addSettingsRow({id, label, type:'seg'|'toggle'|'slider', opts:[[value, text]], get(), set(v), help, section}) lets another module add its own settings row. N.view gets a View row and a VIEW title track automatically.
Saving: N.menus.canSave() -> {ok, reason}, saveManual() (writes the N.save slot plus a copy in 'nostalgia.save.v1.manual'), lastSaved(), openSaveLoad(), openSettings().

Automation: N.menus.quickStart defaults to navigator.webdriver, so PLAY in older tests skips the overwrite prompt and the name card. tests/menus.cjs and smoke.cjs set it to false to drive the real flow. N.menus.debugState() returns the panel stack, focus, map view, journal tab and waypoint for tests.
tests: node nostalgia/tests/menus.cjs passes: 216 checks over desktop (keyboard and mouse), portrait and landscape (touch with CDP drag, pinch and long-press), with zero console, page and N.err errors. It covers title → name card → new game → pause (mission and chase save refusals, Quit mission) → map (pan, zoom, − button, Charminar place card, Route here, right-click or long-press waypoint, legend filter) → every journal tab plus dictionary search and addJournalTab → settings (keyboard, taps, addSettingsRow, persistence) → save → load (manual slot, latest slot untouched) → quit to title (Last saved warning, J-card still fits) → continue (names and money restored). It then plays one cutscene with all 21 step types driven by real input, and checks hold-to-skip, the SKIP pill, abortCutscene, pause inside a cutscene, and that settings survive a reload. Screenshots are in tests/out/menus/.
node nostalgia/tests/smoke.cjs passes (desktop, portrait, landscape). I updated it to drive PLAY → name card → START, and to skip a story prologue with the real SKIP pill if one starts.

Extra one-off checks (not saved as tests): synthetic or gamepad input navigates the pause deck into the map and back; under reduced motion the cutscene VHS effect stays at 0 and the credits page through; a fake N.view shows the VIEW title track and the View settings row; engine_qa's menu-related checks pass (pause/resume, pausing a conversation, ACTION in the pause menu does not advance dialogue).
known_issues: core_systems.cjs (desktop) has 3 failures in checks menus doesn't own. Two expect the old ₹25 starting money, which storycore changed to ₹10. The third expects N.flags to be empty after loading a garbage save; other modules now set flags during reset. Menus no longer writes any flags.

engine_qa contract/bugs runs have 3 failures that are not about menus: 'dateLabel base' and 'clock wraps at midnight' (storycore moved the base date to 2003) and a camera-glide timing check that varies with machine load.
Two must-have ids are not in the world data yet: jubilee_bus_station and bhramaramba_mallikarjuna_theatres. The map will draw them automatically once the world agent adds them.

While I was testing, other agents' half-written src/view3d.js and src/shops.js briefly failed to parse, which made the menus test and smoke fail with 'Unexpected end of input'. The final runs, after both files parsed again, are green.

Some settings are only stored for other modules to act on: autoAdvance (dialogue.js), assist (minigames.js), hintNudges (storycore already reads it), letImmu (missions.js already reads it), captions (hud.js already reads it). The high-contrast and colour-blind body classes need HUD CSS from the HUD owner. On the map, colour-blind mode relies on icon shapes; the colours don't switch to the colour-blind palette yet.
The handwriting font 'Kalam' is injected from Google Fonts at runtime because index.html isn't mine; it falls back to system cursive fonts. Tests stub Google Fonts unless REAL_FONTS=1 is set.
Loading the manual copy needs browser storage. Without localStorage there is only the single N.save slot and the slots panel says so.
Under automation (navigator.webdriver), N.menus.quickStart is on, so PLAY skips the name card unless a test turns it off. Real players always see it.

shops.summary:
The shops, services, side jobs and vehicles work is done and passes its tests. In the last full run, tests/shops.cjs passed all 49 checks with zero console or page errors, and tests/smoke.cjs passed at desktop, portrait-touch and landscape-touch sizes. Screenshots are in tests/out/shops_*.png and I looked at each one.

src/shops.js (about 2,700 lines)
- Every shop and service kind in systems §5 is defined: 53 kinds, each tested to sell. They have prices in paise, opening hours and closed days, menus, and effects: N.player.feed (food), statuses, the Chappal Meter, and time skips.
- All 29 Irani café places (19 cafés plus aliases) serve Irani chai and Osmania biscuits. The ★ combo "Do chai, ek plate Osmania" is ₹8. Holding ACTION orders it without opening the menu.
- Kirana: Mango Bite, khaata (shop credit) at Agarwal-ji's, hiding. Also bakeries, the Gokul Chat panipuri challenge, carts, meat shops (Sunday queue, shopfront only, no buying), medical shops (plaster), photo studios (develop film), internet cafés (₹20/hr, emails, hints), stationery (city map), pindi girnis, barbers (₹10 haircut clears the meter; closed Tuesdays), cycle hire (hourly fee, punctures, overnight fee) and video parlours (brick game, back door).
- Cinemas use made-up film titles, have HOUSEFULL weekends, skip time with a VHS ▶▶ overlay and lower the meter by 2. Prasads stays behind a tin fence until prasads_open. Also the NTR Gardens mini train, Numaish rides, boats, viewpoints, temple prasadam and gurudwara langar, and Rythu Bazaar bargaining (who: 'farmer').
- Stations sell a platform ticket. The weighing machine prints a fortune that points towards the nearest collectible.
- STD/PCO booths save the game and give hint calls: Ammamma, Yadagiri, Vani, Kurnool, and Nanna after 45 finds.
- Buses fast-travel with tickets (Koti, Imlibun and other hubs). Hailing an auto: HORN on foot near a road shouts "AUTO!"; the fare is meter plus ₹10, with a bargain option that opens the bargain minigame (who: 'auto'). Nanna can give a pillion ride on the Chetak.
- The shop card is a clean DOM card that pushes the 'dialogue' state, holds the clock and freezes the meter. Esc or horn closes it. On a phone it becomes a bottom sheet.
- Money never goes below zero; a companion pays (udhaar) and is repaid from your next income. Economy check: about ₹58 earned against ₹54 spent per hour of play.

storycore.summary:
The story core is in place and working. tests/storycore.cjs passes all 99 checks against the live tree, and tests/smoke.cjs passes at all three viewports with zero console errors. Two older engine tests fail some checks because the spec changed what they assert; see known_issues.

What was built:
- **Calendar (`N.calendar`):** a new game starts on TUE 14 JAN 2003. `set` and `jumpTo` move the date; `jumpTo` plays the VHS ▶▶/◀◀ effect with the date spinning on screen and holds the clock and controls for 1.5 s. Midnight rolls over to the next day, and the elastic week loop (systems §10.5) is worked out from the next unfinished main mission. Every date change calls `N.seasons.autoFor(date)`. The date shows on the HUD everywhere the old 1999 date did, with ↻ while the week loops. The clock still runs only in play, and other modules can now freeze it.
- **Tape (`N.tape`):** the ● REC moment shows a blinking ● REC beside the counter, takes ACTION within 8 s (it fires by itself after that) and rolls the counter to the bible value. It also handles the greyed ■ PAUSED state, the declined "● REC?", the biscuit tin, and `play('sideA')` (each J-card line shows while the counter runs to 999).
- **Walkman and home 2-in-1 (`N.walkman`):** cassettes C01–C16 carry the bible text. The RADIO key or the OSD cassette icon moves to the next source (found songs, then the three stations); holding it 0.6 s turns it off. Agent tapes play as Immu's memos. It pauses in respect zones, cutscenes and radio vehicles. The 2-in-1 deck opens at home once a cassette is found.
- **Hints (`N.hints`):** four sources (home/STD, auto, aunty, ask-the-city) and the timed nudges at 3/6/10/15 minutes: tip text, search circle, smaller circle, Immu's PS. There is a Clues page in the Journal.
- **Player:** starts with 1000 paise, tummy 80, drains by activity, and energy can never go above tummy. `feed`, statuses, counted edibles, falling off bikes (DHADAAM!), and a fallback THAK GAYA at tummy 0 if wanted.js doesn't handle it. All of it is saved.
- **HUD:**
  - Additions: the tape counter, a tummy notch with a chai-glass icon that blinks when hungry, a quick-item slot (click or tap to eat), a now-playing strip on the minimap, and hint circles.
  - Sound captions: they follow the menus agent's `captions` setting, which is off by default.
  - Phone clutter: only one toast shows at a time and duplicates merge. Toasts and the district card wait while a banner, J-card or ask card is up.
  - MISSION PASSED card: shows the J-card line and Immu's scribble.
- **Missions:**
  - Walking into a giver now opens the J-card prompt (▶ PLAY on ACTION, or stand in it 1 s; stepping out cancels).
  - Main missions jump the calendar to their bible date and REC automatically if the script doesn't.
  - "Let Immu do it" (or Ayesha / Ammamma) appears after 3 lost tries of the same minigame; a timer gets +25% after 2 timer fails.
  - Kinds main/side/job: one main giver at a time, side givers only in their time window.
  - Per-mission Chappal Meter policy and saves refused during missions.
  - Also fixed: a giver used to restart its mission right after a quit.
- **Audio:** Birla Mandir no longer has bells (wind, distant hum, soft steps on marble). All the new SFX are in, including the `dappu` teenmaar roll, which also replaces the bell at Bonalu. `hitec` and `cantonment` versions of the day theme play by district. The walkman has its own volume dip. No azaan or chants anywhere.

collectibles.summary:
I rewrote src/collectibles.js (about 1,700 lines, replacing the stub). It implements bible §6 and systems §7 in full. tests/collectibles.cjs passes all six sections (data, reach, play, rewards, save, visual) with zero console errors, and tests/smoke.cjs passes.

- **The five series:** 12 kites, 30 golis, 16 cassettes, 12 tickets and 24 frames (23 riddles plus the story's F24) make 93 finds. Every name, spot, hint, kite tail tag, cassette dedication or memo and stage riddle is copied from the bible. The 35 trivia cards are the bible's verified facts (12 ticket backs and 23 prints). There are also 4 extra story cards, also verified: the mummy, Mozamjahi's clock faces, Birla Mandir having no bells, and the Veiled Rebecca.
- **Placement:** every position is worked out at runtime from place or landmark ids, so it survives map changes. It is then checked: walkable, not water, not on the road, never in a respect zone, inside the map. A blocked spot moves to the nearest valid cell. The test confirms all 94 positions (93 plus F24) connect to the player's spawn by walking.
- **Hiding techniques:** behind tall buildings (the pseudo-3D walls cover them), on a roof (C13 sits on the home terrace via the roof zones, or at the stair foot if there are none), under tree canopies, behind bus-stop boards, inside shops via an ACTION "Look …" that only works while the shop is open, on the riverbed sand, and on or beside boulders (K10 rides the buffalo boulder). Kites can also be tied up high (hangar rib, Kakatiya arch). Time gates: C10 only on Sundays 07:00–20:00, C11 after M2, K6 moves and F09 opens on 25 Jul.
- **Feedback:** a glint twinkles every 3.5 s within 90 u, with a small light pool at night. The hot/cold beacon beeps within 120 u, and a faint minimap ring appears near (not on) the item. Both only work for unlocked series and both have settings toggles. A pickup gives a sound, a toast like "GOLI 7/30 · Red swirl", a 10-sparkle burst and a counter that flashes under the HUD money/energy column.
- **Frame riddles:** stand within 40 u, face the subject within 60°, outside respect zones, and ACTION shows "Click (F07)". A viewfinder overlay appears for 0.6 s with the camera pulled toward the subject and the HUD hidden, then the flash. The actual view is saved as a small warm-toned photo that shows up in Nanna's album. F07 can also be clicked from a boat. Developing takes two game days or until the next mission.
- **Viewpoints:** reaching one zooms the camera out to 0.55 for 3 s, then unfound items within 900 u blip on the map for 180 s. The walk-up ones fire after about 1 s standing there, in free roam only.
- **Rewards and ladder:** every per-series reward is in, and the total-finds ladder at 5/12/20/30/45/60/75/93 sets the `N.flags.unlock_*` names that vehicles.js and shops.js already read. Each step toasts at once; the family line plays when you next walk in at home (Salim-bhai's at Café Gulistan for 93). Golis 30 also draws a marble pouch on Chinnu's sprite.
- **Integration:** cassettes go to `N.walkman.add`. There are six Journal tabs with "!" badges, two settings rows, a debug fallback list (`N.debug.collectibles()`) and `N.save` persistence.

The story agents' API is documented at the top of the file. Screenshots are in /home/user/DS/nostalgia/tests/out/collectibles/.

audio.summary:
I built N.audio, the game's full sound layer, and installed it as src/audio.js, replacing the 796-byte stub; no other agent had written real code there. Everything is synthesised live with WebAudio: no samples, no external files. It passes tests/audio.cjs against the real game with zero console errors. The engine's smoke test also passes on desktop, portrait and landscape with it loaded, with whole-game update at 0.10-0.16 ms per frame.

Limits on verification: headless Chromium has no speakers, so I could not listen to anything. Quality checks were indirect: spectrogram sheets I inspected, loudness levels, compiled notes decoded back to note names, and an automated harmony check. That decoding caught a real bug: every chord part (pads, strings, brass, e-piano) was transposed to the wrong key and clashed with the melodies. It is fixed. Engine and radio were tested with a stand-in vehicle object, because src/vehicles.js is still a stub. The HUD toast is also a stub, so radio DJ text is stored but not yet shown.

What it contains:
- **96 sound effects.** Every sound on the brief is in, plus Hyderabad street and festival sounds (kulfi cart bell, dial-up modem, Laad Bazaar bangles, koel, crows, cow, Begumpet jet, fireworks). Sounds placed in the world get quieter, panned and duller with distance. Up to 22 sounds can play at once, with per-sound cooldowns.
- **Engine sounds.** Each vehicle type has its own: Chetak and RX100 two-stroke putt with simulated gear changes, the auto's rattle, the Ambassador's hum, the bus and lorry diesel, the cycle's freewheel ticking. They cover the player's vehicle and the two nearest traffic vehicles.
- **Ambience.** Background mixes for each district style blend as you move, with water near the lake and crickets at night. Pressure cookers peak at mealtimes and birds at dawn. About 90 place rules drive these, covering every must-have place (Koti bus stand horns, Gokul Chat sizzle, temple bells, both stations, girni thump, Irani cafe cups, school bells, playground cricket, STD booths, barbers, video parlours, internet cafes). A song drifts out of the RTC X Roads theatres and the Numaish waltz plays near the exhibition. Ganesh immersion, Bonalu, Ramzan, Numaish and Sankranti soundscapes switch on from N.flags.
- **Music: 12 original tracks.** Title theme "Yaadon Ki Gully", day, night, chase, Old City qawwali (claps, and the tempo speeds up each round), tension, victory, festival, Numaish, kites, a cassette-style flashback, and the Charminar ending "Charminar Ki Chaon". The ending is about 2 minutes in five sections: a quiet sitar opening, the title melody returning, a rise, a key-change lift, and a slowing close. Instruments are sitar, santoor, tanpura and mandolin (plucked-string synthesis), bansuri, shehnai, harmonium, strings, brass band, tabla, dholak, dappu and marfa drums, and 90s synths.
- **Automatic music choice.** Title screen gets the title theme, and a new game opens on it for about 40 seconds. Free roam picks day, night or Old City music, rests between plays, and waits 10 seconds before changing at district borders. Chappal Meter 3 or more switches to chase music, which holds 4 seconds after escaping. A mission pass plays a fanfare, then the victory track. The radio and Walkman take over from the score. Dialogue lowers the music; pause muffles the world.
- **Radio.** Three fictional stations, each with two fictional songs, short jingles and Hinglish DJ dedications: Deccan Vani 101.2 "Aapki Farmaish", Band Baaja 93.5 and Pop Patang 104.8. Stations keep playing while you're away, so you tune in mid-song. Switching gives static; output goes through a small-speaker filter.
- **Walkman.** Plays cassette songs with tape wobble and hiss.

Additions beyond the brief, because both story pitches are built around a cassette: "● REC" a city sound, play the recorded sounds back as a montage, a "■ STOP" that makes the music slow to a halt like a tape deck, and a hot/cold beeping beacon for tracking hidden things.

Other choices:
- **Respect at religious sites.** I did not synthesise the call to prayer or any chant. Mosques get pigeons and cooing; temples and churches get bells.
- **Stamina.** Running out of energy plays panting rather than the full "THAK GAYA" sting.
- **Old stub calls.** Other modules can keep calling the stub's names (`music('id')`, `play()`, `stopMusic()`, `volume`, `radio.toggle()`); all still work.

CPU and memory:
- **Main thread.** About 0.05 ms per frame in a 20-second play run; one-off spikes of 3-7 ms when a new track starts.
- **Audio thread.** Estimated 3-5% of one desktop core for the busiest track.
- **Fixes along the way.** Profiling led to three changes: pre-rendering drum hits, cheaper pitch and filter automation, and preparing tracks and string sounds in idle time after unlock.

I also added section 17 to ARCHITECTURE.md documenting the API, the music rules, the events listened to and the CPU approach. My dev tools are in staging/: a lab page plus a script that draws spectrogram sheets into the git-ignored tests/out/audio_lab/.
api_notes: Unlocking: menus should call N.audio.unlock() inside the START gesture. The first pointer or key press anywhere also unlocks, and later presses resume a context the OS suspended (iOS phone calls). Before unlock every call is a safe no-op.

Sound effects: N.audio.sfx(name, {x, y, vol, pitch, pan, surface, variant, delay, force, ui}) returns true or false. Pass world x/y for positional sounds; omit them for UI sounds. All names are in N.audio.SFX_NAMES (96). Other modules can also emit the 'sfx' event with {name, x, y}.

Volume settings: setVolume(bus, 0..1) and getVolume(bus) for master, music, sfx, radio or ambient; mute(bool), toggleMute(), muted. Saved in localStorage key 'nostalgia.audio.v1'. Emits 'audio:settings'. The menus settings screen should call these.

Story music cues: music.play(id) locks a track (music(id) also works); music.lock(null) or music.stop() releases it. music.mood(id) is a softer request that chase music can override. A mission object can carry a .music track id. music.sections(id) and music.position() let cutscenes sync to the score.

Charminar finale: call N.audio.music.play('ending'), then listen for the 'music:ended' {id} event to roll credits. The ending's sections start at about alaap 0 s, theme 16.6 s, rise 46.6 s, lift (key change) 75.6 s, coda 103.9 s.

Track ids: title, flashback, day, night, chase, oldcity, tension, victory, ending, festival, numaish, kites. Radio songs: r_chandni, r_barish, r_baraat, r_neon, r_pager. Station jingles: id_vani, id_band, id_pop.

Radio: next(), set(i or -1), off(), toggle(); read on, station, text and STATIONS. Vehicles can set TYPES[type].radio true/false; the default gives radios to autos, cars, buses and lorries. A vehicle remembers its station in v._radioStation. Emits 'radio:station' {station, name}. DJ lines go to N.hud.toast.
Walkman: unlock(songId) when a cassette is collected; play(id), stop(), next(), rewind(); read library and playing. Song titles and artists are in N.audio.SONGS.

Cassette framing: rec(sfxName) for '● REC'; tapeMontage([names], {gap}) returns a Promise and plays the collected sounds back like Side A; tapeStop(sec) returns a Promise and makes the score slow to a halt. tape(0..1) adds cassette wobble to the music and also follows N.render.fx.vhs automatically. The 'flashback' event plays the rewind sound.
Clue hunting: beacon(target {x,y}, entity or placeId, {sound, max}) beeps faster and higher as the player gets close; beacon(null) stops it.

Events audio already listens to: horn, bump (the {a,b,speed} payload from entities.js), pickup/collectible {kind}, money {delta}, mission:start, mission:complete, mission:fail, objective, hud:objective, wanted and wanted:change, busted, wasted, player:exhausted, dialogue:open, dialogue:close, dialogue:char {speaker}, player:enterVehicle/exitVehicle (it also polls N.player.vehicle), footstep {surf}, kite:cut, radio:next, shop:buy, door {kind:'wood'}, splash, save, game:new, game:quit, music {id or mood}.

landmarks.summary:
I replaced the src/landmarks.js stub with real pseudo-3D art (about 3,400 lines). All 50 heritage and worship draw ids from map_plan §4a now have their own art, which covers all 113 landmarks of those types. The brief also listed five civic ids that the map plan gives to places_art.js; I drew those too (Mozamjahi Market, the three railway station variants, LB Stadium, Begumpet terminal and control tower). places_art.js loads after this file, so if it registers the same ids, its version replaces mine.

The gallery test shoots all 120 landmarks at noon and at night and passes with zero console, page or N.errors entries. tests/smoke.cjs still passes, and the map_preview engine teleports to the key places with no errors.

**Recognisability (checked on the screenshots):**
- **Charminar (the finale):**
  - Granite plinth and the great-arch storey with all four faces detailed (pointed arches with daylight showing through, rosettes, clocks that show the in-game time).
  - A projecting first-floor balcony ledge, the arcaded upper storey and an arched crest.
  - A light well over the crossing of the arches and the small mosque with its domes on the west of the roof.
  - Four fluted minarets with two corbelled balconies, arched kiosks and onion domes on lotus petals; the back minarets are drawn in layers so they sit correctly behind the upper storey.
  - Paving and an iron railing on the plaza, and pigeon flocks that scatter when the player comes close.
  - At night: a warm floodlit glow, glowing arches and clock faces, and twinkling bulb outlines. On festive nights (the Chand Raat flags, or `N.landmarks.fx.festive`) green and white bulb strings run from the minarets to the plaza corners, with crescents on each face.
- **Old City:** the four Char Kaman arches over the road (piers with guard chambers, domed kiosks; you can walk underneath), the Gulzar Houz fountain with moving water, and Mecca Masjid (a granite hall with 3 x 5 domed roof bays, five great arches and the massive octagonal corner columns).
- **Hill temples and the lake:** Birla Mandir is white marble on the Naubat Pahad rock, with a curved main tower, two side shrines, a hall, a gateway tower, steps and a saffron flag. The Buddha is on the Gibraltar Rock island, standing on a lotus pedestal with the raised hand. The Tank Bund statues are bronze figures on plinths with ornamental lamps, lit at night.
- **Big public buildings:** the Assembly (white, central dome, chhatris, Indian flag), the Public Gardens buildings, the High Court in red and white stripes, Osmania General Hospital, the State Central Library and the Salar Jung Museum. Large blocks get real courtyard light wells.
- **Golconda and the tombs:** curtain walls with merlons and round bastions, Fateh Darwaza flanked by bastions, the Bala Hissar ruin on its rock, and Qutb Shahi tombs with ribbed domes on arcaded cubes.

places-art.summary:
I created src/places_art.js (about 4,100 lines). It gives pseudo-3D art to all 67 civic, transport, market, cinema and everyday draw ids in map_plan §4b, which covers 306 landmarks. It also adds 27 decorations built from place data: 18 colony playgrounds, NTR Gardens and 8 street markets. Everything is data-driven from landmark draw ids and fields (face, sign, sign2, films/film, variant, solids) and from place kinds and parks, so new map entries pick up art automatically. The two must-haves the map reconciler added since the brief (recording_centre_1 and electronics_shop_1, both video_parlour variants) and Café Noor-e-Iran already have art.

**Test result:** tests/places_gallery.cjs finishes with 207 screenshots and zero page, console or N.errors entries. It shoots one landmark per draw id, the must-have showcase ids, every decoration and the story variants, at noon and at night. I looked at the screenshots and the zoomed crops and reworked anything that did not read well. tests/smoke.cjs still passes, and the map_preview engine teleports to the bus termini, RTC X Roads, NTR Gardens and Prasads all land exactly on their place points.

**What is drawn:**
- **Koti bus stand, Rathifile and Mehdipatnam:** a shelter on red posts with route-number boards, parked red city buses that are solid in the collision grid, crowds and conductors.
- **Imlibun (MGBS):** the terminal with vaulted roof shells and a "MAHATMA GANDHI BUS STATION" sign, platform canopies, and express, deluxe and luxury buses showing KURNOOL, WARANGAL, TIRUPATI and VIJAYAWADA.
- **Gowliguda hangar:** a steel barrel vault with buses inside; its roof fades when you walk under it.
- **Gokul Chat:** a steel counter with a glass box of puris, a steaming ragda pot and pani cans, a kulfi matka stall, parked scooters, and a crowd that peaks in the evening.
- **RTC X Roads cinemas (Sandhya twin halls, Sudarshan, Odeon, Devi, plus five others):** hand-painted hoardings with stylised hero and heroine faces and only fictional titles, ticket-queue cages that fill before show times, cycle stands, marquee bulbs at night, and two free-standing film hoardings.
- **Restaurants:** Bawarchi, Paradise and the others get biryani degs and queues; during Ramzan the Old City hotels get haleem bhattis.
- **Prasads IMAX, three variants:**
  - **Fence:** tin fence, a concrete frame with a turning crane, and a "PRASADS / COMING SOON / THE GIANT SCREEN" hoarding.
  - **Opening day:** "OPENING TODAY" banner, balloon arch, bunting and a crowd.
  - **Open:** the giant-screen block with a curved glass front and a PRASADS sign.
- **NTR Gardens, two variants:** open shows the concrete Machan tree with dining decks and a spiral stair, the waterfall, the moving mini train, Nandi statues and flower beds. Work in progress shows red soil, the bare trunk in scaffolding, saplings, a digging JCB and a hoarding.
- **Rythu Bazaars:** tin sheds over the farmers, vegetable heaps left visible, hanging balances and price slates.
- **Numaish:** a domed gate with bulbs, striped stalls with names (Delhi Papad, Kashmir Shawls and so on), a tilted giant wheel that turns with light chasers, and the maut ka kuan with a motorbike circling the wall. Out of season everything is shuttered and still.
- **Schools:** a corridor facade facing the ground, a gate arch with the initials (S.V.M.), a fluttering tricolour, a gate vendor (ice-gola cart in summer), and kids by the school bell and on Sunday.
- **Shops:** kirana, stationery, pindi girni (thumping chakki, belt and pulley, flour puffs and dust), barber (scrolling pole), cycle rent, video parlour, photo studio, medical (green cross), meat shop (hen cages and a Sunday queue, no gore), internet cafe, bakeries, bangle shops and Cherma's. Each has a fitted signboard with a pictogram, an awning, goods on the footpath, a shopkeeper and customers.
- **Irani cafes:** teal or cream arched fronts, some with tiled roofs, marble-top tables with bentwood chairs, glass jars of Osmania biscuits, and chai steam.
- **Pushcarts:** banana, flower (jasmine and marigold heaps, garlands), samosa, dosa/idli, coconut, chai, kite and book stalls, with vendors and petromax lamps at night.
- **Small street furniture:** STD ISD PCO booths with a lit pulse meter, and bus stops with the stop name split at place-name suffixes (HIMAYAT / NAGAR).
- **Colony life:** playground equipment (swings, slide, see-saw, merry-go-round), a gully cricket game with an animated bowler and ball, and Ganesh pandals in season. The home has a terrace with a Sintex tank, antenna, cot, saris on the line, chillies and kites, plus a rangoli at the gate and kites flying at Sankranti. The friend's house is a variant.
- **Other civic art:** water tanks; GPO with post boxes; hospitals with ambulances; colleges; the library; Ravindra Bharathi; Ramakrishna Math; Bal Bhavan; the AIR mast; the Doordarshan tower; Gachibowli stadium; the Monda, CTC, Murgi Chowk and fruit markets; film studios; Secunderabad Club; Ameerpet coaching centres covered in C/C++/JAVA/ORACLE banners; Trendz; HITEX (construction or open); the zoo, Shilparamam and University of Hyderabad gates; Lumbini jetty; the musical fountain; the dhobi ghat; Dhoolpet idol workshops; the parked plane; and the suburban halts.

core-A.summary:
The engine for NOSTALGIA is built and tested, and the smoke test passes at desktop 1280x720, phone portrait 390x844 and phone landscape 844x390 with zero console errors. It boots in about 0.8 s on the real map (which now has MAP_PLAN_FINAL, about 24k structures and 463 places), runs at 60 fps in headless Chromium, and a phone-size frame costs about 4 ms of JavaScript.

What it covers:
- **Core:** utilities, seeded random numbers, events, a systems registry where every call is error-wrapped, a state stack, game time, and a day/night clock that starts at golden hour.
- **Controls:** keyboard, gamepad and touch. Touch has a floating joystick on the left, ACTION/RUN/HORN on the right and MAP/PAUSE at the top. The ACTION button shows the context label (a desktop "E — label" prompt does the same), and page scroll/zoom is blocked.
- **Rendering:** a crisp pixel canvas with whole-number scaling that refits on resize and rotation. The camera has look-ahead and zooms out with speed, and buildings lean outward like GTA2. Also: drawing helpers for walls, domes, cylinders and signs, a crisp pixel font for shop signs, a time-of-day colour tint, and night lighting with sodium and tube-light pools, lit windows and porch bulbs. Screen shake and a VHS effect are there for cutscenes.
- **World:** roads with footpaths, black-and-yellow kerbs, painted medians, zebra crossings and clean junctions. Water has sandy banks, depth shading and moving glints; parks, plazas and maidans have their own textures. Buildings are generated per district style, with many trees, lamps and 3D Deccan boulders. Collision, road lookups and a road network with left-hand lanes are in place for traffic.
- **People and player:** ten looks (kid, uncle in lungi and banian, aunty in saree, burqa, school uniform, police and more) with a walk cycle. The player walks and runs with stamina, slides along walls, and gets a small marker after a few idle seconds so they're easy to find on a phone.
- **Boot, debug and build:** title → play flow, pause when the tab is hidden, and hot-reload support. All the debug hooks other agents' tests rely on are present. The build makes a standalone page and an artifact fragment; both run with no errors.
- **Stubs:** every other module has a safe placeholder so the game runs end to end. The menus stub gives a title screen with START, a pause screen and a slow camera drift over the city behind the title.

**The map file:** the map agent replaced my placeholder `worlddata.js` with the real map while I was working; I didn't touch their file. I also added their new `src/world_extras.js` (railways) to `index.html` right after `world.js`, as its header asks; it works with the engine.

**Performance work:** the first version took about 29 ms per frame in dense areas. Caching roof tops, tree canopies and window grids, and baking static shadows into the ground, brought dense areas down to 2–5.5 ms of JavaScript. World build went from 1.06 s to about 0.3 s by indexing roads and spacing checks.

**Screenshots:** in `tests/out/`; I looked at all of them across day, golden hour and night.
api_notes: Main loop deviation: the update is semi-fixed, not strictly fixed. Each frame's time (capped at 0.1 s) is split into equal sub-steps of at most 1/60 s, so motion stays smooth at 60/120/144 Hz. N.time.now only advances in play, dialogue, cutscene, minigame and gameover modes. N.perf gives fps, frameMs, updateMs and drawMs.

New N.game API in main.js: newGame({skipIntro, hour, minute}), continueGame(), quitToTitle(), pause(), resume(), snapshot(). newGame resets everything and emits 'game:new' with the options. The story module must listen for 'game:new' and run the intro unless skipIntro is set. Other events: 'game:continue', 'game:quit', 'game:pause', 'game:resume', 'boot', 'world:built'.

Menus own the pause key (the stub does it in a 'menus' system at order 85). Real menus must call N.audio.unlock() inside the START click, then N.game.newGame({skipIntro:false}) or N.game.continueGame(). The engine calls N.menus.title / pause / resume / hideAll / isOpen.

Systems: N.systems has list, get, init, update, draw, reset. runIn ['*'] means every mode. Re-adding an id replaces it. Added order bands: entities 25, interact 58, menus 85. N.state.set(mode) replaces the whole stack; N.state.has(mode) checks it.

New N.interact decides what ACTION does. Use add(id, {x,y or entity, r, label, priority, enabled, use}), remove(id), or call offer({label, priority, dist, use}) every update step, e.g. 'Ride Chetak' near a vehicle. The interact system (order 58) picks the best, shows its label on the button/prompt, and runs use() when ACTION is pressed. Systems that read ACTION themselves run earlier and must consume it.

Entities system (order 25): calls update(dt) on every entity except ones flagged selfUpdate (the player has its own system). It pushes overlapping solid actors apart by mass (also supports fixed, noCollide, ignore), calls onBump(other, {a, b, nx, ny, speed}), and emits 'bump' above speed 30. main.js calls N.entities.draw(), and each in-view entity's draw() queues itself. N.Actor is the base class.

People are drawn 1.5x their collision size (N.people.SCALE) so they're readable. N.people.randomLook(rng, kind) makes a random look. Player extras: look, anim, exhausted, god, teleport(x, y), reset(), serialize()/deserialize(). Events: 'footstep' {x, y, surf, run, who}, 'player:exhausted', 'player:teleport'.

Rendering extras: N.render.follow (entity to follow), camOverride {x, y, zoom, rate, snap} for cutscenes, snapCamera(), warmChunks(x, y, r), fast projection helpers k/sx/sy, distKey for sorting buildings, screenToWorld and clientToWorld. The ground painter is handed a context already translated to world coordinates. Draw helpers leave the canvas transform reset to identity. N.render.night (0..1) says how dark it is.

More draw helpers: quadPath, rectPath, visibleWalls, plane(h, fn), pixelText(x, y, h, str, color, {scale, shadow, rot}) with pixelTextWidth/pixelTextCanvas, and castBox/castPoly/castCircle/castPole for moving shadows. Box style accepts roofFn and wallFn; cylinders accept grad:false and bands; domes accept steps, bulb and finial. Lights are {x, y, r, color, intensity, h, glow}.

Shadows of static buildings, trees, rocks, walls and lamps are baked into the ground tiles using a stepped sun position; N.render.shadowEpoch changes about every 11 game-minutes and stale tiles repaint two per frame. N.render.sun holds the sun direction and shadow offset.

Map data rules: a landmark's x, y is its CENTRE (w = east-west, d = north-south). Optional fields honoured: landmark plaza, solids, noSolid and solid:false; water bank and color; building color, roof and sign; park surface:'sand'; road median and road trees. Extra tree kinds: coconut, mango, tamarind, peepal (unknown kinds draw as neem). Places and spawn points are kept clear of generated buildings.
Each frame world.js calls N.landmarks.enqueue(lm, visible) for landmarks within the view plus 140 units, and N.landmarks.paintGround(ctx, lm) when painting ground tiles.

Extra N.world queries: surfaceSpeed(surf, mode), findFree(x, y, mode, maxCells), randomRoadPoint(rnd, kinds), queryStructures(x0, y0, x1, y1, fn), addStructure({t:'custom', x0, y0, x1, y1, draw}), and renderMap(pixelsPerUnit), which returns a cached map image for the minimap and full map.

Road network (N.world.roads): nodes carry links, inc (all touching roads), deg and w; edges carry lanes, oneway and kind. Functions: isJunction, edgeBetween, neighbors, nearestNode, randomRoute(from, steps, {rng, avoid, prev}), and laneOffset/lanePoint, which put traffic in the LEFT lane. nearestRoadPoint returns {x, y, dist, road, seg, t, angle}.

Input extras: N.input.analog (movement came from a stick, so vehicles should steer toward it), hold, press(a, sec), setMove(x, y, analog=true) and setMove(null), clear, anyPressed, setLabel(action, text) such as RUN to BRAKE, showTouch, and an 'input:device' event. Touch controls only show in play mode. HUD agents should keep about 120x52 px at the top-right free on touch for MAP/PAUSE.

Page layout: canvas#game, then #ui for the HUD (clicks pass through unless a part has class 'interactive'), then #touch, then #overlay for menus and dialogue (full-screen panels use .screen and show with .show), then #debug. body[data-mode] mirrors the game mode. Scrollable panels must use the .scroll class, the only place touch can scroll. The HUD should store the current objective in N.hud.objectiveText so N.debug.state() can report it.

Debug extras: N.debug.perf() and freezeClock(on). teleport also accepts a landmark id and returns the final {x, y}, or null if unknown or not a number. state() also reports clock, day, district, surface, wanted, and player energy, money and vehicle. Overlay keys with #debug: backquote toggles it, Alt+1..4 jump to 07:00 / 12:00 / 17:30 / 21:00, Alt+G toggles god mode.

index.html now loads the map agent's src/world_extras.js right after world.js; it is in ARCHITECTURE §3. Any new src file must be added to index.html or it won't ship. Tests replace Google Fonts with an empty response so runs work offline; REAL_FONTS=1 loads them through the proxy.
tests: node nostalgia/tests/smoke.cjs: SMOKE PASSED at all three sizes (1280x720 keyboard, 390x844 touch, 844x390 touch). Each run checks: boot, no page scroll, title START click/tap, real keyboard or touch-joystick movement (an in-page odometer recorded 116–172 units walked), the ACTION label showing and firing once, pause and resume, 3–6 teleports, night at 21:00 (night overlay 1.0), rotating the phone re-fits the canvas, and zero console, page or engine errors.
Smoke frame time over 3 s in-page: desktop 16.6 ms per frame at 60 fps with 1.8–2.1 ms of JavaScript; portrait 60 fps with 4.0 ms; landscape 60 fps with 2.8 ms.

node nostalgia/tools/build.mjs: 24 scripts inlined, about 365 KB each for dist/nostalgia.html and dist/artifact.html. The build itself checks that script tags still open and close correctly. Both files loaded in Chromium (the fragment wrapped like a host page), started from the title, moved with the keyboard, and showed no errors.

Hot reload: both the hot.data path and the hot.ready(start) path restore play mode, position, money, clock and flags, and hot.snapshot() returns the state. With no hot runtime the game boots to the title.

Soak test: a full day/night time-lapse at 120 game-minutes per second, 24 teleports with walking and running, plus shake and VHS. No console warnings or errors and no engine errors; 116 shadow refreshes went through without problems.
Visual review of draw helpers (boxes, polygons, cylinders, domes, discs, text, pixel text, sprites) from four camera positions at zoom 2: hidden walls are correctly skipped and shading is consistent.

Real-map districts reviewed in screenshots: Old City and the Charminar ring, Tank Bund and Hussain Sagar, the Musi with bridges and sandy banks, HITEC, Abids/Koti, Secunderabad barracks and the colonies, at noon, golden hour and 21:00.
known_issues: Headless Chromium draws with a software renderer, so the fps figures reflect that and real phones haven't been measured. JavaScript draw time is 2–5.5 ms per frame on this desktop CPU in the densest views; mid-range phones may be 2–3x slower, so dense Old City views at full zoom-out while driving could drop below 60 fps.
Teleporting builds the surrounding ground tiles all at once, which causes a single 50–80 ms hitch. This is deliberate so there's no pop-in after a jump.
The landmarks stub draws plain labelled cream boxes until the landmarks agent replaces it. Most of the real map's landmarks currently look like that.
The window grids on walls use an approximation that can be off by up to about 1 pixel at the extreme screen edges.
Lit windows at night are drawn on top of the darkness layer, so in rare cases near the screen edge a far building's lit windows can show through a nearer building.
Shadows move in small steps (about 2.6° roughly every 11 s at normal clock speed) instead of smoothly, and stale ground tiles refresh two per frame.
The map agent's railways (world_extras.js) are painted on top of the baked shadows, so tracks don't show building shadows. This is cosmetic.
Gamepad support is written but untested, since headless Chromium has no gamepad.
Tests use fallback fonts because Google Fonts is stubbed; real fonts only load in a normal browser or with REAL_FONTS=1.
My placeholder map no longer exists in the repo because the real map replaced it. A copy lives only in my scratchpad for engine testing.
world.js keeps two small developer aids: N.world.detail (switches for profiling) and N.world.buildPhases (build timings).
core-A.perf: JavaScript work per frame comes from the in-page perf counter; all runs held 60 fps unless noted. Desktop 640x360 canvas: about 2 ms at the spawn and about 3 ms in the dense Old City. Phone portrait 390x844: about 4 ms at the spawn and 4.6–5.5 ms in the densest districts. Before optimisation the dense views cost about 29 ms. Ground tile paint costs about 0.4 ms each in JavaScript. World build is 0.30–0.40 s for about 24k structures (down from 1.06 s); boot to the title is about 0.8 s.

core-B.summary:
I built vehicles, HUD, dialogue, missions, save and a DEMO mission, and they all work together. My new tests/core_systems.cjs passes all 83 checks at desktop, phone portrait, phone landscape and with browser storage disabled. Core A's smoke test still passes at all three sizes. Neither suite logged a console or engine error, and the single-file build still runs.

**Vehicles:** all 12 types have arcade handling (acceleration, braking, reverse, steering that depends on speed, handbrake drift with skid marks, slowdown on dirt and sand). Walls stop them with a bounce, sparks and spin; vehicles shove each other and push people aside. Each type has distinct pseudo-3D art that leans like GTA2 buildings: windscreens visible from above, the yellow-and-black auto, the red CITY BUS with a route number, the lorry's HORN OK PLEASE board, bikes with riders, and a striped boat with a foam wake on the water. At night they show headlight pools and tail lamps. Tested with real key presses:
- Several types accelerate, steer, brake and let you get in and out.
- A car stops at a building wall without passing into it.
- The boat never leaves the water.
- You can't walk through a parked car.
- Borrowing an occupied auto makes the driver jump out shouting and adds one slipper to the Chappal Meter.
- The touch joystick steers toward the stick direction.

**HUD:** VHS-style clock and date, tin-sign money, energy bar, a five-slipper Chappal Meter that shakes when it rises, an objective/timer/toast column, MISSION PASSED/FAILED banners, a GTA-style district card, and a minimap with blips, edge arrows and a pink route line along the roads. The test checks that nothing overlaps itself or the touch buttons at 390x844 and 844x390.

**Dialogue:** typewriter text, highlighted slang with a meaning line underneath, choices by keys, number keys or tap, and pixel-art portraits drawn from a description of the character, with five moods.

**Missions:** markers are a pulsing cylinder of light, with an off-screen arrow showing the distance. Walking into a giver starts its mission. The DEMO mission "Chai Before Sunset" runs end to end: talk to Saleem bhai at the cycle stand, rent a cycle, race a 45-second timer to the Irani café, then get the reward and an autosave. If the timer runs out you get MISSION FAILED, and Retry puts you back at the race start, already on a cycle.

**Save:** save, reload the page, Continue restores money, flags, clock, day, finished missions, position and the vehicle you were riding. Corrupt or partial saves fall back to a backup copy or are ignored without errors. Without browser storage it saves to memory for the session.
api_notes: Vehicle type sizes: w is the LENGTH along the heading and d is the WIDTH (local +x forward, +y right). Extra type fields: short, verb, cls ('bike'|'car'|'auto'|'heavy'|'boat'), mode ('drive'|'boat') in place of 'surfaces', reverse, drag, turnLow/turnHigh, steerResp, drift (grip with the handbrake), bounce, mass, camZoom, smoke, rider, door, lights. N.vehicles.define(id, {base:'rx100', ...}) adds story vehicles.

N.vehicles.spawn(type, x, y, angle, opts) takes {color, color2, seed, driver: true|{look}|Actor, controller(v, dt), locked, label, special, route, beacon, seeded}. Vehicle fields: speed (signed forward u/s), slip, throttle, ctl {throttle, steer, handbrake, brake}, driver, controller, asleep, locked (player can't get out), noEnter, lightsOn, taxi. Vehicles are entities with selfUpdate and noCollide; the 'vehicles' system (order 30, runs in play/dialogue/cutscene) moves them and handles every collision involving a vehicle.

Traffic AI hook: set v.controller = (v, dt) => { fill v.ctl }; vehicles.js does the physics and collisions. Vehicles with no driver and no controller brake to a stop and then sleep, costing nothing. People hit by a vehicle get knockT (seconds) plus a velocity kick, and a 'bump' event {a: vehicle, b: ped, speed, ped: true}.

Controls: keyboard is tank style; when N.input.analog is true the vehicle steers toward the stick (stick pointing behind = brake, then reverse). RUN is the handbrake and its touch button is relabelled BRAKE / H-BRAKE. Exiting puts you at the left door first, then right, rear, front; boats need a shore within reach.

ACTION priorities: 'Ride Chetak' / 'Drive auto' / 'Borrow auto' are offered at priority 0 within 18u of the vehicle body; 'Get off' / 'Get out' while driving is also priority 0. Shops and NPC talk should use priority 1 or higher to win. The mission 'Retry mission' offer uses priority 5.

Events emitted by vehicles.js: bump {a, b|null, speed, x, y, wall?, ped?, vehicle}; horn {x, y, type ('foot' when walking), vehicle, who, dur}, repeated while a car or bus horn is held; vehicle:enter|exit {vehicle, actor}; player:enterVehicle|exitVehicle; radio:enter|exit {vehicle}; vehicle:borrowed {vehicle, driver, by, x, y}; vehicle:spawn; sfx {name:'skid'}. Borrowing calls driver.onEvicted(v, by) when the driver is an Actor; otherwise a simple angry-driver ped with a speech bubble is spawned. Either way the Chappal Meter goes up by one via N.wanted.add(1).

Pre-placed vehicles: N.vehicles.autoSeed is true by default. On game:new / game:continue it parks cycles at cycle_rent places, two boats at lumbini_jetty, and the family Chetak about 58u west of the home spawn (seeded: true). traffic.js can set autoSeed = false. Other helpers: nearest(x, y, r, pred), distTo(v, x, y), exitSpot(v), remove(v), clearDecals().

N.hud additions: banner(title, sub, ms, {kind: 'pass'|'fail'|'busted'|'chapter'|'info'}); the kind is inferred from the title if omitted, and pass/fail/busted cut in front of title cards. blip(id, {x,y}|entity|placeId, {color, icon: dot|star|giver|shop|square|ring|diamond, label, pulse, route, size, minimap:false, edge:false}). timer(label, sec, {countdown}), timer(null) and timerValue(). ask(title, [{label, key, fn}]) returns a close function; closeAsk(). For the full-map agent: blips (a Map), blipPos(b), route() (the current route polyline) and mapImage(). objective() emits 'hud:objective'.

N.dialogue additions: define(id, {name, color, look, portrait(ctx,w,h,mood) | false, voice}). Unknown speaker ids get a generated speaker; 'narrator' (no portrait) and 'you' (Chinnu) are built in. paintPortrait(ctx, w, h, look, mood) look fields: skin, hair, hairStyle (short|side|long|bun|braid|bald|spiky|puff|curly|oiled), moustache, beard, specs, cap, dupatta, burqa, bindi, shirt, stripes, tie, earrings, flowers, age, bg, kind. Moods: neutral|happy|angry|sad|surprised. say(s, t, {mood, auto}); choice(s, prompt, opts, {default}) returns the index, or -1 if cancelled; play(lines) returns the last choice; cancel(), advance(), isOpen(), current, textSpeed, skip. It pushes the 'dialogue' state only when opened in play mode. Events: dialogue:open|close|line|char|choice.

Mission definition extras: giver {place|npc|x,y, r (default 14), onFoot}, when(), reward {money, item, flag}, passText, color, autosave, onPass(). m extras: toast, marker/unmarker, vehicle(type, x, y, a, opts), data, attempt, retrying. until(fn, {timeout, failMsg}) fails the whole mission on timeout even when it isn't awaited. timer(sec, label, {failMsg}) returns {stop, add, left}. give(id, {name}) shows a 'Got: name' toast. N.missions also has lastFailed, isDone, giverPos, posOf, complete(), fail(reason), abort() (silent), retry() and markers() (for the full map). The save section is 'missions'.

Retry from a checkpoint: Retry re-runs the script quickly up to the same m.checkpoint(name). goto, wait, until, say, cutscene resolve at once; choices and minigames replay the recorded answers; money and give are skipped. Spawns, flags, objectives and blips are applied normally. The player is then teleported to the checkpoint and put back into a vehicle of the same type. Story scripts must make the same decisions each time before a checkpoint (no randomness there).

N.save.load() checks the data first, then aborts any mission, cancels dialogue, clears flags, calls N.systems.reset() and restores each section separately. It emits 'save:loaded'. save({reason, toast:false}) emits 'save'. info() returns a summary for a Continue button. Built-in sections: player (including the vehicle being ridden), clock and flags; missions registers itself in its init(). The previous good save is kept under 'nostalgia.save.v1.bak', and saves are held in memory when localStorage throws.

story.js DEMO (marked as replaced by the story agent): mission 'demo_chai_run' with its giver at giver_himayatnagar, speakers 'saleem' and 'cafe', and an intro toast on game:new unless skipIntro is set. It uses cycle_rent_5 and irani_cafe_3.

I changed none of Core A's code or test files. ARCHITECTURE.md gained implementation notes for vehicles, HUD/dialogue, missions and save, plus a line about the new test in the testing section. style.css gained '=== hud ===' and '=== dialogue ===' sections.
tests: node nostalgia/tests/core_systems.cjs: CORE SYSTEMS PASSED, 83 of 83 checks, zero console, page or engine errors.

Desktop vehicles with real keys: cycle, chetak, auto, ambassador and bus each get in on ACTION, accelerate on W (for example the ambassador reached 111/165 u/s and moved 81u), steer right on D (0.4 to 0.75 rad), brake on S, and get out beside the vehicle. The camera zooms out with speed (0.967). Horn events fire for every type.

Walking into a parked car is blocked at its body. Borrowing an occupied auto spawns the driver ped, fires vehicle:borrowed and raises the Chappal Meter to 1. The boat sailed 194u and never left the water.

review-core.summary:
I reviewed the core engine against ARCHITECTURE.md §5-§13, probed it for bugs, measured performance, checked screenshots and the build, and fixed what I found. Everything now passes: smoke (42 checks), core_systems (83), the other agents' suites (audio, landmarks_gallery, map_preview), and my new suite `/home/user/DS/nostalgia/tests/engine_qa.cjs` (365 contract checks plus 48 bug probes, perf, visual and build sections). The build is 1.3 MB and runs from file:// with no errors.

Most important fixes:
- **Frozen player after a load:** if a conversation was cancelled while paused (for example a load from the pause menu), resuming dropped into an empty dialogue mode and the player could not move. Fixed with a new `N.state.remove(mode)`.
- **Camera wobble:** snapping the camera to whole pixels made the car you're driving shake about 1 screen pixel every frame. Scrolling is now accurate to the screen pixel; measured shake fell from 1.71 to 0.85 screen pixels, the physical limit.
- **Stuck controls:** touch buttons and the joystick stayed held after switching apps or tabs, or when the finger lifted elsewhere. They now release.
- **Pausing mid-conversation:** a hidden tab now pauses during dialogue, ACTION on the pause menu no longer advances the text, and the dialogue box no longer draws on top of the pause screen.
- **Walls and exits:** a car ramming a person against a wall pushed them into it (4 of 10 runs). Getting out next to a thin wall could put you on the far side. Removing a boat mid-lake left the player standing in water. All three are fixed.
- **Contract bugs:** `randomRoute({rng})` / `randomRoadPoint` crashed with `N.util.rng` objects, and `speakers[id] = {...}` crashed portraits. Both now work as documented.
- **NaN values:** a NaN position counted as walkable and never cleared once it got into the player, a vehicle or the camera. They now recover and are logged.

On tunnelling: I couldn't make it happen on the original code (900 crashes into 1-3 cell walls, four directions, up to 900 u/s). I still added sub-stepped vehicle movement as a safeguard; it costs about 24 µs per step for 40 vehicles.

The `core_systems` wall test was failing about a quarter of the time on any code, because cars that hit a wall at an angle slide along it. It now picks only flat walls hit head-on (0 failures in 120). The smoke test broke because the minigames agent added an antenna interaction next to the home spawn; the test's own interaction now takes priority.

Contract additions are documented in ARCHITECTURE.md: `N.state.remove`, `N.input.releaseAll`, `N.entities.pushTo`, `N.render.PAD/subpx/stats.ms`, `N.world.stats`, `N.debug.perf().ms`, pause allowed during dialogue, and missions closing their minigame or cutscene when they fail.
fixed: world.js: randomRoute(from, steps, {rng}) and randomRoadPoint(rnd) threw 'rnd is not a function' when passed an N.util.rng(seed) object (the contract's rng). Both now accept a function or an rng object.

world.js: surfaceAt(NaN, NaN) read grid[NaN], so isWalkable(NaN, NaN) returned TRUE and NaN positions looked valid. Non-finite coordinates are now VOID, and collide() with non-finite input returns {hit: true, bad: true}.

render.js: camera wobble. Snapping the camera to whole internal pixels made the followed vehicle shake ±0.5 internal px (about 1 screen px) every frame. The canvas now has 1 internal px of padding and is shifted by the sub-pixel remainder in whole device pixels (CSS translate). Measured frame-to-frame shake: 1.71 -> 0.85 device px (0.85 is the device-pixel limit).
render.js: a NaN camera value, follow target or override stuck forever. The camera now recovers.

input.js: only the keyboard was released on blur. Held touch buttons, gamepad and joystick stayed down after an app or tab switch. Added releaseAll(), called on window blur and when the tab hides (synthetic test holds are kept).

input.js: the joystick stuck when pointer capture was lost or the finger lifted outside the zone without capture. Added a lostpointercapture handler and page-level pointerup/pointercancel fallbacks for the joystick and buttons.
main.js: hiding the tab mid-conversation did not pause, because pause() only worked in play mode. It now works in play and dialogue, and resume returns to the conversation.

dialogue.js: the dialogue kept typing and took ACTION and number keys under the pause menu, so ACTION on the pause screen advanced the conversation. It now only runs in play/dialogue/cutscene/minigame/gameover. Lines with an auto-advance time now count game time, not real time.
style.css: the dialogue box drew above the pause screen and stayed clickable. It is now hidden while paused, on the map or in the journal.

core.js + dialogue.js: a dialogue cancelled while paused (e.g. a load from the pause menu) left a stale 'dialogue' state under 'paused', so resume froze the player. Added N.state.remove(mode); the dialogue uses it when it closes.
dialogue.js: the documented N.dialogue.speakers[id] = {name, color, portrait} assignment crashed when drawing the portrait. Such speakers are now normalised on first use.
missions.js: a failed or aborted mission left its minigame (and cutscene) open. The runner now calls N.minigames.abort('mission:<result>') and N.menus.abortCutscene() if present.
entities.js: player.deserialize turned junk fields into NaN position or money (affects the hot-reload path). Junk fields now keep current values.
entities.js: teleport and save-load to out-of-map coordinates left the player at -500,99999. Positions are now clamped into the map, with a fallback to the spawn.
entities.js: the player now recovers from a NaN position or velocity (last good spot, logged as player.nan).

vehicles.js + entities.js: a car ramming a person against a wall pushed them into the wall (4 of 10 runs), and vehicle-vehicle and actor pushes ignored walls. Added N.entities.pushTo (pushes stop at walls) and a vehicles shove() that collides with walls; a person pinned against a wall now stops the car instead.

vehicles.js: the exit spot could be on the far side of a thin wall the car was parked against. Exits must now be reachable from the vehicle without crossing a wall, with a fallback ring search around the body.
vehicles.js: a forced exit (e.g. despawning the boat under the player mid-lake) left the player standing in water. It now finds the nearest dry land.

vehicles.js: added sub-stepped movement (no collision circle moves more than ~70% of its radius per piece) plus restoring the last good position if a circle centre ends inside a solid. NaN steering/throttle from controllers now reads as 0, non-finite vehicle state is recovered, and spawn() rejects non-finite positions. This also stopped an audio.js 'non-finite AudioParam' error triggered by entering a NaN vehicle.

render.js perf: ground-chunk builds are now time-budgeted (2.5 ms per frame, at least one), stale-shadow repaints limited to one per frame, and one chunk is prefetched ahead of travel every third frame. The worst-frame chunk cost fell from 8.7 to 1.5 ms (portrait) and from 4.6 to 0 ms (desktop).

render.js/main.js/debug.js/world.js: added per-phase frame timings (N.render.stats.ms, also in N.debug.perf().ms) and sprite-cache-miss counters (N.world.stats).

tests/core_systems.cjs: the wall-stop check failed about 25% of the time on any code (the same 15 of 60 with the old physics) because cars hitting a wall at an angle slide along it. It now picks walls that are flat and hit head-on, measured to 1u (0 failures in 120). The assertion is unchanged.

tests/smoke.cjs: the new antenna minigame interaction beside the home spawn made the bare ACTION tap start a minigame and hide the touch controls. The test's interaction now has priority 99 and the uncontrolled tap is gone.
remaining: Landmarks (landmarks.js, landmarks agent) are the biggest cost in dense views. Per frame: Osmania Hospital ~585 µs, Charminar ~400, High Court ~380, Birla Mandir ~350, Assembly ~270; their night light layers add 270-560 µs each. They should cache static parts (roof sprites / Path2D) the way world.js does.

Portrait night stress test (40 lit vehicles, 180 u/s through Old City zoomed out to 0.78, software rendering) still runs ~10-11 ms of JS per frame. Buildings cost ~12 µs each with 180-320 on screen; I found no further cuts without visible level-of-detail loss.

Tunnelling was not reproducible on the original code (900 runs, 1-3 cell walls, 4 directions, up to 900 u/s); the chain of collision circles already caught it. The sub-stepped movement is a safeguard costing about 24 µs per step for 40 vehicles.
Roof sprite cache misses average 2.3 per frame (0.25 ms) at speed, with occasional bursts of 8-10 roofs (~1.5 ms). These could be prefilled in quiet frames.

audio.js (audio agent) does not guard against non-finite x/y in playSfx; setValueAtTime threw when a NaN vehicle was entered. The engine now prevents NaN vehicles, but audio should sanitise its inputs too.

Menus stub (menus agent): Esc does nothing during a dialogue because the stub only reads pause in play/paused (pausing when the tab hides does work). N.menus.abortCutscene() also still needs implementing.
All fps figures come from headless Chromium with software rendering; real phones are unmeasured.
N.entities.remove() splices the list during the update loop, so an entity removed by another entity's update skips one entity's update that frame. Minor; left as is.
The residual 0.85 device-pixel camera shake is the device-pixel limit and cannot be reduced further.

§10 says menus own the pause key, but the stub's pause handling runs only in play/paused, so Esc/PAUSE does nothing during a conversation. N.game.pause() itself now supports dialogue mode.
